author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read Wazuh 4.x manager alerts from alerts.json, sent as JSON over syslog to the data collector. Authentication alerts go to Auth, and every other alert goes to the third-party alert schema with a severity from rule.level.
notes:
Setup:
- Wazuh 4.x managers; Wazuh 5.0 removes syslog output.
- On the manager, add a syslog_output block with the data collector as server and <format>json</format>, run wazuh-control enable csyslogd and restart the manager.
- The manager sends each alert from alerts.json over UDP 514 with the tag ossec.

Field mapping:
- Alerts in the authentication_success or authentication_failed rule groups go to Auth, with the Windows Security logon fields mapped.
- Every other alert, brute force and lockout correlations included, goes to the third-party alert schema with the rule description as title and a severity from rule.level: 0 to 3 INFO, 4 to 7 LOW, 8 to 11 MEDIUM, 12 to 14 HIGH, 15 and up CRITICAL.

Time:
- The event time is the alert's own timestamp with its offset.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples are made up in the alerts.json layout Wazuh documents.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 (163 of 163 fields matched the emulator), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there.
- Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent.

Known gaps:
- OSSEC's JSON output has a different layout and isn't covered.
- The tenant's built-in sshd parser also matches alerts whose full_log is an sshd line, as does the library's OpenSSH entry.
- In a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 the built-in parser took those lines in 7 of 15 Run Tests.
- Expect some of those alerts to keep the built-in mapping.
